info.title: Ambivo Workforce API
info.description:
**Ambivo Workforce** is time and attendance: shift definitions, a roster, a clock
log, and the attendance register payroll reads. It runs inside the Ambivo Core API
(`ingress.ambivo.com`) and shares its auth, tenancy, access control and response
envelope. There is no separate Workforce service.

## The model: template → occurrence → outcome

| Entity | What it is | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `work_shift` | The **template**. Has no date. | "Cafe Morning, 06:00–14:00, Mon–Sat" |
| `shift_assignment` | One **occurrence** for one person. The roster row. | "Maria works Cafe Morning on 2026-08-24" |
| `punch_event` | The **raw log** of clock events. | "Maria clocked in at 06:04 from the front counter iPad" |
| `attendance_day` | The **outcome**, computed from punches. Payroll reads it. | "Maria: 7h 45m worked, 15m late, 0 OT on 2026-08-24" |

A fifth, `shift_change_request`, carries an employee asking the employer to change
a future roster row. A sixth, `time_off`, carries days a person is away from work.
Approved time off keeps that person off the roster. A crew (`/user/workforce/crew`) is a named group of people at
one site.

**The register is computed from the punch log.** `POST /user/attendance_day/process`
writes each `attendance_day`. A supervisor changes a day only through the
`/user/attendance_day/manage` actions `adjust`, `approve`, `unapprove`,
`approve_overtime`, `unapprove_overtime`, `lock` and `unlock`.
Re-processing a day leaves `manual_adjust_minutes` as it was.
`payable_minutes` is `worked_minutes + manual_adjust_minutes`, never below 0.

## Response envelope

A Workforce refusal is HTTP **200** with `result: 2`. Branch on `result`:

```json
{ "result": 1, "shift_assignment": [ ... ], "total_count": 12 }
{ "result": 2, "error_code": "SHIFT_ALREADY_STARTED", "error": { "message": "..." } }
```

Other statuses come from the platform: 401 without a valid token, and 403 while
the tenant account is pending review. An unhandled error is HTTP 200 with
`result: 2` and `status_code: 500` in the body. On the REST routes
(`/list`, the record routes, `/user/time_off`, payroll export), the
`/user/workforce/*` routes and the crew routes it is instead
`{"result": 2, "error": "Internal error", "error_code": "INTERNAL_ERROR"}`.
There `error` is a string and there is no `status_code`. The sign-in
endpoints also answer some refusals at 400, 401, 403 (`BOT_DETECTED`) or 429.

Records are keyed by **entity name**: `work_shift`, `shift_assignment`,
`punch_event`, `attendance_day`, `shift_change_request`, `time_off`, `crew`.

Most writes need the tenant's Workforce Pro feature: creating and editing shift
definitions and shifts, clocking, minting a badge, raising a change request,
processing the register, and creating and editing crews. Without it the write
answers `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO` at HTTP 200.

## Authorization

Three rules apply together.

* **`module_access`** (from the caller's roles) decides whether a caller may do a
  thing at all, for example `shift_assignment: ["C","R","U","D"]`.
* **Record ownership** decides which rows a list returns. Roster rows, punches,
  register days and change requests are owned by the employee (`userid` =
  `employee_userid`). Lists of roster rows, punches and register days return the
  caller's own rows and the rows of people below them in the role tree. The
  change request queue is described on its own route. A tenant admin gets only
  their own rows on these lists. `/user/workforce/roster` reads a whole site.
* **Workforce scope** (`GET /user/workforce/me`). A supervisor is a tenant admin or
  a caller whose roles grant `U` on `shift_assignment`. A caller whose roles name
  sites acts only at those sites, and lists leave out other sites' rows apart from
  the caller's own. Roles are read from the database on every request.

Shift definitions are created readable by the whole tenant (`access_dict`
`{"*": ["R"]}`). Writing one needs `work_shift` privileges.

On a tenant with role hierarchy off, Workforce treats only a real admin as a
supervisor: someone holding a role with wildcard `module_access` or
`role_purpose: admin`. Nobody on such a tenant is limited to sites.

Three roles are seeded: `workforce_manager`, `workforce_supervisor`,
`workforce_employee`. `workforce_employee` has `R` on `work_shift`,
`shift_assignment`, `punch_event` and `attendance_day`, and `C` and `R` on
`shift_change_request` and `time_off`.

**Clocking yourself never checks `module_access`.** `POST /user/punch_event/clock`
checks `C` on `punch_event` only when `employee_userid` names someone else.
`workforce_employee` has no `C` on `punch_event`, so an employee clocks only
themselves. A manual punch (`POST /user/punch_event`, or `/manage` `add`) needs
`C` on `punch_event`, also for yourself.

## Dates and timezones

`shift_date_str`, `work_date_str` and `punch_date_str` ("YYYY-MM-DD") are the day
keys. The epoch fields beside them are for sorting and range reads.

A roster row's timezone is resolved when the row is written: the row's own
`timezone`, else the shift definition's, else the tenant's `timeZone`, else
`America/Los_Angeles`. When the first zone found is unrecognised, the tenant's
`timeZone` is used, then `America/Los_Angeles`. `start_ts` and `end_ts`
are stored then, so a later edit to the shift definition does not move rows
already written.

A shift whose `end_time <= start_time` **crosses midnight**. Its `shift_date_str`
stays the day it started. A punch matched to a roster row is filed under that
row's `shift_date_str`. A punch with no roster row is filed under its local date.
The zone is the punch's own `timezone`, else the tenant's, else
`America/Los_Angeles`.

## Biometrics

`verification: device_biometric` records that the handset's own Face ID or
fingerprint check passed. The client sends that value. No image or face template
is sent. A self-service clock or badge may claim `none`, `selfie`,
`device_biometric`, `pin` or `access_code`. `card`, `face` and `fingerprint` are
accepted only from `/user/punch_event/ingest`. The `/manage` `add` action and
`POST /user/punch_event` accept them for a punch for someone else.

post.summary: Create, update, delete or list shift templates
post.description:
`action`: `add` | `update` | `delete` | `get` | `get_entity_ids`.
`update`, `delete` and a single `get` name the row with a top-level
`work_shift_id`.

Writes need `C` / `U` / `D` on `work_shift` and are site scoped (see
`DELETE /user/work_shift/{id}`). Reads need no privilege.

**Delete is guarded.** A definition used by any shift or register day is
refused with `WORK_SHIFT_IN_USE`. A batch delete (`ids_list`) answers
`{deleted_ids, refused: [{work_shift_id, error_code}], deleted_count}`.

`start_time` / `end_time` accept `HH:MM` (seconds are dropped) or a minute
count, and are stored as `start_time_min` / `end_time_min`. A blank time is
refused with `WORK_SHIFT_START_TIME_MIN_REQUIRED` or
`WORK_SHIFT_END_TIME_MIN_REQUIRED`. Send both times on `add`. A time
left out is 00:00, so leaving out both makes a 24-hour shift.
An empty number field is stored as 0.

`geofence_radius_m` is 0 (the default) or at least 161. A new or changed
value from 1 to 160 is `WORK_SHIFT_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_TOO_SMALL`. A value
that is not a number is `WORK_SHIFT_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_INVALID`.

Other refusals: `WORK_SHIFT_NAME_REQUIRED`, `WORK_SHIFT_CODE_DUPLICATE`,
`WORK_SHIFT_BREAK_EXCEEDS_SHIFT`, `WORK_SHIFT_ROUNDING_MINUTES_UNSUPPORTED`,
`WORK_SHIFT_OT_DAILY_THRESHOLD_REQUIRED`,
`WORK_SHIFT_OT_WEEKLY_THRESHOLD_REQUIRED`,
`WORK_SHIFT_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_REQUIRED`,
`WORK_SHIFT_GEOFENCE_LOCATION_REQUIRED`, `WORK_SHIFT_TIMEZONE_INVALID`,
`WORK_SHIFT_NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_WORK_SHIFT`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`,
`SITE_CODE_INVALID`, `WORK_SHIFT_PEOPLE_NEEDED_INVALID` (with `data`
`{min, max}`), `WORK_SHIFT_ID_REQUIRED`, `WORK_SHIFT_ID_INVALID`,
`WORK_SHIFT_IN_USE_CHECK_FAILED`, `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION`,
`WORK_SHIFT_STATUS_INVALID`, `WORK_SHIFT_ROUNDING_MODE_INVALID`,
`WORK_SHIFT_OT_BASIS_INVALID`, `WORK_SHIFT_OT_MULTIPLIER_NEGATIVE`,
`WORK_SHIFT_DAYS_OF_WEEK_INVALID`, `WORK_SHIFT_DAYS_OF_WEEK_OUT_OF_RANGE`,
`WORK_SHIFT_BREAK_LIST_INVALID`, `WORK_SHIFT_BREAK_LIST_OUT_OF_RANGE` and
`WORK_SHIFT_BREAK_KIND_INVALID`.

A time that cannot be read is `WORK_SHIFT_START_TIME_MIN_INVALID` or
`WORK_SHIFT_END_TIME_MIN_INVALID`. An hour over 23, a minute over 59, or a
count outside 0 to 1439 is `WORK_SHIFT_START_TIME_MIN_OUT_OF_RANGE` or
`WORK_SHIFT_END_TIME_MIN_OUT_OF_RANGE`. A number field that is not a
number is `WORK_SHIFT_<FIELD>_INVALID`, and a negative one is
`WORK_SHIFT_<FIELD>_NEGATIVE`, for example
`WORK_SHIFT_GRACE_IN_MINUTES_NEGATIVE`.

A list read caps `page_size` at 200.

post.summary: Create, update, delete or list roster rows
post.description:
`action`: `add` | `update` | `delete` | `get` | `get_entity_ids`.
`update`, `delete` and a single `get` name the row with a top-level
`shift_assignment_id`.

Writes need `C` / `U` / `D` on `shift_assignment`
(`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT`). A caller whose roles name sites
writes only rows at those sites (`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`).

A payload may write only these fields: `employee_userid`, `work_shift_id`,
`shift_date_str`, `timezone`, `site_code`, `status`, `assignment_type`,
`cancel_reason`, `notes`, `tags`, `latitude`, `longitude`,
`geofence_radius_m`, `require_geofence`, `require_photo`,
`require_biometric`, `auto_clock_out`, `job_title`, `meta`,
`custom_form_dict`. Other keys are dropped.

**One shift's own times.** `add` and `update` also read `start_time` and
`end_time`, together: `"HH:MM"` (seconds allowed and dropped) or minutes
after midnight, as wall time on `shift_date_str` in the row's `timezone`.
An end at or before the start ends the next day. The row then has
`times_overridden: true` and the minutes in `start_time_min_override` and
`end_time_min_override`, and `start_ts`, `end_ts` and `scheduled_minutes`
come from them. Lateness, early departure and timesheets read those. The
shift definition is not changed. `use_definition_times: true`, or both
times empty, goes back to the definition's times. On `update`, a new
`work_shift_id` with no times also goes back to the new definition's
times. A new `shift_date_str` keeps them as wall times on the new day.
Refusals: `SHIFT_TIMES_BOTH_REQUIRED`, `SHIFT_START_TIME_INVALID`,
`SHIFT_END_TIME_INVALID`, `SHIFT_TIMES_SAME`, `SHIFT_TIMES_TOO_LONG` (more
than 16 real hours, counted across a clock change),
`SHIFT_TIMES_SHORTER_THAN_BREAK` (not longer than the unpaid break),
`SHIFT_TIMES_ALREADY_PROCESSED` (the register counted the row),
`SHIFT_TIME_DOES_NOT_EXIST` (the start or the end falls in a spring-forward
gap on its day, for example 02:30 on a day the clocks go from 02:00 to
03:00), and the overlap check below. A time the autumn change repeats
is its first occurrence, in summer time. A definition's own times keep
the old rule: a start in the gap lands after it (02:30 reads as 03:30).

When an `update` moves the window of a `published` or `confirmed` row that
has not ended, the person gets one push and websocket notice, "Your shift
times changed", about a minute after the last edit. Each edit stages a
`tenant_tasks.call_api` task to `POST /admin/workforce/shift_times_notice`
a minute out and retracts the one before it. When it runs, the server
reads the row again and sends nothing when the times equal what the person
was last told, the row is gone, cancelled, a draft or ended, or it now
belongs to someone else. No notice is staged when the same update gave the
row to someone else. The notice is in the person's `preferred_language`
(`PUT /user/data`; the Workforce app sends the language it shows), else
the tenant's `language_code`, else English. An English that the person
never saved (every user starts with `en`) gives way to a Spanish or
Turkish tenant language: saving `preferred_language` stamps
`preferred_language_set_ts`, and only then does English count as chosen.
It is written in English, Spanish or Turkish. The shift reminder is set again for the new start.

The server sets `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `scheduled_minutes`,
`unpaid_break_minutes`, `work_shift_name` and `employee_name`. `site_code`,
`job_title`, the location, `require_geofence`, `require_photo`,
`require_biometric` and `auto_clock_out` are copied from the shift
definition unless the payload sends them.

A sent `employee_userid` must be an active user of the tenant
(`EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`). `employee_userid` is required only for a caller
whose roles name sites (`EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND` when missing). For anyone
else, `add` without it creates a row with no employee, owned by the
caller. A shift overlapping another non-cancelled shift of the same employee is
refused with `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_OVERLAP`. A unique index over non-cancelled
rows refuses the same person on the same definition on the same day
(`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_DUPLICATE`). A shift dated inside the employee's
approved time off is refused with `ON_LEAVE`; an update is checked when
it changes the date, the person, or brings a cancelled row back
(`TIME_OFF_CHECK_FAILED` when time off could not be read). A definition that belongs to a site is used
only at that site (`SITE_TEMPLATE_MISMATCH`).

Other refusals: `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS_NOT_ALLOWED` (only the register sets
`completed`), `CANCEL_REASON_REQUIRED` (a change to `cancelled` without
`cancel_reason`), `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_ALREADY_PROCESSED` (editing or deleting a
row the register used), `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_FIELD_NOT_WRITABLE` (a change to
`userid` or `access_dict`), `SITE_CODE_INVALID`, `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_BUSY`,
`WORK_SHIFT_ID_REQUIRED`, `WORK_SHIFT_NOT_FOUND`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_DATE_INVALID`, `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS_INVALID`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_TYPE_INVALID`, `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_ID_REQUIRED`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_ID_INVALID`, `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND`,
`WORK_SHIFT_ID_INVALID`, `EMPLOYEE_LOOKUP_FAILED`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_OVERLAP_CHECK_FAILED`, `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION`. A
`geofence_radius_m` that is not a number is
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_M_INVALID`, and a negative one is
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_M_NEGATIVE`. A `latitude` or
`longitude` that is not a number is `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_LATITUDE_INVALID`
or `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_LONGITUDE_INVALID`. This route drops
`tenant_id` from the payload. `PATCH /user/shift_assignment/{id}` refuses a
change to it.

Changing `employee_userid` moves the row's owner to the new employee and
withdraws the previous employee's pending change requests on the row.
Deleting a row closes its pending change requests as `shift_removed`
with `closed_reason: shift_deleted`. A
batch delete (`ids_list`) answers `{deleted_ids, refused, deleted_count}`.
A list read caps `page_size` at 500 and sorts by `start_ts`.

post.summary: Assign crew. Create shifts for people or a crew over a date range
post.description:
People are `employee_userid_list` plus the crew's members who are active
users, read at request time (`crew_id`), with duplicates removed. An id in
`employee_userid_list` that is not an active user refuses the whole call
with `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`.

A crew's site is used when `site_code` is omitted. A different `site_code` is
`CREW_SITE_MISMATCH`. An archived crew is `CREW_ARCHIVED`, a crew with no
active members is `CREW_HAS_NO_MEMBERS`, and a crew at a site the caller
does not manage is `CREW_NOT_FOUND`.

Days: `pattern`, or `days_of_week` (0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday) when `pattern`
is absent. With neither, the shift definition's own days. With a
top-level `days_of_week`, a day the shift definition does not run on is a
`skip` row with `OUTSIDE_DAYS`. This applies only when the definition
names its days. The same days sent as `pattern: {type: weekly,
days_of_week}` are created, with no `OUTSIDE_DAYS` check.

`pattern` shapes:

| `type` | Fields |
|---|---|
| `weekly` | `days_of_week` |
| `rotating` | `days_on`, `days_off`, `anchor_date_str` (default `from_date_str`) |
| `alternating` | `work_shift_ids` (2 or more), `cycle_days` (default 7), `days_of_week`, `anchor_date_str` |
| `custom` | `dates`. Dates outside the range are ignored. |

**Partial success.** Every person × date gets a row with an `outcome`:
`create`, `skip` or `fail`, and a `reason_code` when not created:

| reason_code | Outcome | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ALREADY_ON_A_SHIFT` | `skip`, or `fail` when `skip_existing: false` | An overlapping shift exists, or an earlier row of this request takes the time. |
| `NOT_AT_SITE` | `skip` | The person works at other sites and not this one: every one of their roles that names a site names another, and they have no shift here in the last 14 or next 27 days. A person whose roles name no site is at every site. A tenant admin is at every site, and on a tenant with role hierarchy off everyone is. |
| `OUTSIDE_DAYS` | `skip` | See above. |
| `ON_LEAVE` | `skip` | The person has approved time off that day (`time_off`). |
| any other code | `fail` | A create that was refused, for example `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_STATUS_NOT_ALLOWED`. |

Created shifts default to `status: draft` and `assignment_type: regular`.
Every created shift carries `recurrence_group_id`, and for a crew `crew_id`
and `crew_name` (a snapshot). Publish them with
`POST /user/shift_assignment/publish` `{"recurrence_group_id": "..."}`.

**Idempotency.** Send a `client_request_id` (a UUID per tap of Save). The
same id with the same body returns the first response with `replayed: true`
and creates nothing. The same id with a different body is
`CLIENT_REQUEST_ID_REUSED`. A retry within 5 minutes while the first is
still running is `GENERATE_IN_PROGRESS`. Ids are per user and kept 7 days.
A refused request does not use up its id.

**Limits.** At most 180 days and 2000 person × date rows. Past either, the
whole call is refused with `GENERATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and `data`
`{max_days, max_rows, day_count | row_count}`. Nothing is written.

**Headcount.** `staffing` has one entry per date and shift definition in the
request: `people_needed` (the definition's, null when none), `people_after`
(distinct people on a non-cancelled shift of that definition that day,
counted again after the writes) and `short_by` (`people_needed -
people_after` when above zero, else 0). People are counted at the request's
site, or the shift definition's site when none is sent, or at every site
when neither has one. A day the definition does not run on (`OUTSIDE_DAYS`)
is left out. Short days are never refused.

Needs `C` on `shift_assignment`. A caller whose roles name sites generates
only at those sites.

Whole-call refusals: `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT`,
`WORK_SHIFT_ID_REQUIRED`, `WORK_SHIFT_ID_INVALID`, `WORK_SHIFT_NOT_FOUND`,
`EMPLOYEE_LIST_REQUIRED` (no people and no crew), `SITE_TEMPLATE_MISMATCH`,
`SITE_CODE_INVALID`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `DATE_RANGE_INVALID`,
`NO_APPLICABLE_DATES` (the pattern gives no dates),
`SCHEDULE_PATTERN_INVALID`, the `PATTERN_*` codes and
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_OVERLAP_CHECK_FAILED`. `ROSTER_GROUP_NOT_SAVED` means rows
were created but not all were tagged with `recurrence_group_id`.

`message` reads "Rostered N shift(s)". Its "N already rostered" part
counts every skip, including `NOT_AT_SITE`, `ON_LEAVE` and
`OUTSIDE_DAYS`.

200.description: Envelope with rows and counts, or a refusal

post.summary: Preview what Assign crew would do, without writing
post.description:
Same body as `/generate` (`client_request_id`, `status` and
`assignment_type` are ignored). With neither `employee_userid_list` nor
`crew_id` the response is dates only (`pattern_type`, `slot_count`,
`slots`) and needs no privilege. A range over 180 days is then
`DATE_RANGE_TOO_LARGE`. Other refusals: `DATE_RANGE_INVALID`,
`WORK_SHIFT_ID_INVALID` (missing or malformed `work_shift_id`),
`WORK_SHIFT_NOT_FOUND`, `NO_APPLICABLE_DATES`, `SCHEDULE_PATTERN_INVALID`
and the `PATTERN_*` codes. On this path a `days_of_week` that is not a
list is ignored.

With people or a crew it also returns `rows`, `create_count`, `skip_count`,
`fail_count`, `crew_id`, `crew_name` and `staffing`, computed as generate
computes them, and needs `C` on `shift_assignment`. In the preview,
`people_after` is the people on the roster now plus this preview's `create`
rows. Its refusals are those of `/generate`, including
`GENERATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` for a range over 180 days.

post.summary: Copy one site's week of shifts to another week, as drafts
post.description:
Reads the 7 days from `from_date_str` at `site_code`. Every shift there
that is not cancelled and has an employee is copied, drafts included.
Each copy lands on its own date plus the gap between `from_date_str` and
`to_date_str`. A gap that is not a multiple of 7 moves shifts to other
weekdays. A target week in the past is allowed.

Each copy keeps the person, the shift definition, `assignment_type`, the
shift's own times when `times_overridden`, and the crew. Notes, tags,
`job_title`, the location and the geofence, photo and biometric settings
come from the shift definition again. Copies are `draft`, share one
`recurrence_group_id`, and are created through the manage `add` path.
Publish them with `POST /user/shift_assignment/publish`
`{"recurrence_group_id": "..."}`.

Every source shift gets a row with an `outcome`: `create`, `skip` or
`fail`. Skip reasons: `DEFINITION_INACTIVE`, `PERSON_INACTIVE`,
`NOT_AT_SITE`, `ON_LEAVE`, `ALREADY_ON_A_SHIFT`. A failed row carries
the create's own refusal code, or `CREATE_FAILED`.

`client_request_id` works as on `/generate` and shares its store, kept 7
days. A preview does not use it.

Needs `C` on `shift_assignment` and Workforce Pro, also for a preview.
The site must be registered, and one of the caller's sites when their
roles name sites.

Refusals: `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT`,
`WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, `SITE_CODE_REQUIRED`, `FROM_DATE_INVALID`,
`TO_DATE_INVALID`, `SITE_CODE_INVALID`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`,
`COPY_WEEKS_OVERLAP` (the target starts within 6 days of the source,
either way), `GENERATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (over 2000 source shifts, with
`data` `{max_days, max_rows, row_count}`),
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_OVERLAP_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMPLOYEE_LOOKUP_FAILED`,
`TIME_OFF_CHECK_FAILED`, `CLIENT_REQUEST_ID_REUSED`,
`GENERATE_IN_PROGRESS`, `ROSTER_GROUP_NOT_SAVED`.

from_date_str.description: First day of the week to copy. Any weekday.

to_date_str.description: First day of the target week. Defaults to 7 days after `from_date_str`.

preview.description: Answer the rows and write nothing. Only `true` or the string "true" count. `1` or "yes" writes the copies.

200.description: Envelope with `rows`, `from_date_str`, `to_date_str`, `site_code`, `create_count`, `skip_count` and `fail_count`. A write also returns `recurrence_group_id`, `created_ids` and `created_count`, plus `client_request_id` when one was sent and `replayed: true` on a replay. `message` reads "N shift(s) to copy", also after a write.

reason_code.description: On a row that was not created

to_date_str.description: First day of the target week

post.summary: Move draft rows to published
post.description:
Targets, combined when more than one is sent: `ids_list`,
`recurrence_group_id`, or `site_code` with `shift_date_str` (every draft at
that site that day). With no target, or only one of `site_code` and
`shift_date_str`, the call is `PUBLISH_TARGET_REQUIRED`.

Only `draft` rows change. Matched rows in other statuses are counted in
`skipped_count`. A caller whose roles name sites is refused with
`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED` when any matched row is at another site or at no site.

Needs `U` on `shift_assignment`. An unparseable id in `ids_list` refuses the
whole call with `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_ID_INVALID`. A bad `shift_date_str` is
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_DATE_INVALID`.

post.summary: The roster board. One date range, grouped by date
post.description:
Reads the caller's visible rows (the same scoping as the list route) for
`from_date_str` to `to_date_str`, at most 42 days. `match_filter_dict`
adds conditions, but its `shift_date_str` is replaced by the range.
Refusals: `DATE_RANGE_INVALID`, `DATE_RANGE_TOO_LARGE`
(with `max_days`). `page_size` defaults to 500 and is capped at 500.
`total_count` is counted on page 1 only. On page 1, `truncated` is true
when `total_count` is larger than the rows returned. On later pages
`total_count` is 0 and `truncated` is false.

200.description: Envelope with rows grouped by date

by_date.description: Keyed by `shift_date_str`, each a list of roster rows

post.summary: Put a substitute on someone's shift
post.description:
Creates a **second row** for the substitute. The original is cancelled
(`cancel_reason` is `reason`, or "Covered by substitute") and gets
`covered_by_assignment_id`. The cover row has `assignment_type: cover`,
`replaces_assignment_id`, the original's site, and `status` (default
`published`).

A substitute with approved time off that day is refused with `ON_LEAVE`,
and the original stays as it was.

If the cover cannot be created, the original is restored and the refusal is
returned.

Needs `U` and `C` on `shift_assignment`, at the row's site. Refusals:
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT`, `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_ID_INVALID`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_BUSY`,
`SUBSTITUTE_USERID_REQUIRED`, `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_ALREADY_PROCESSED`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_ALREADY_CANCELLED`, `SUBSTITUTE_SAME_AS_EMPLOYEE`,
`EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`, `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_NEEDS_ATTENTION` (the restore
failed).

post.summary: One day's roster joined to what actually happened
post.description:
Who was due in, who came, who is on the clock, and who is working with no
roster row. Omit `shift_date_str` for today in the tenant's timezone.
Cancelled rows are left out.

Rows carry recorded times and clock state only. No elapsed or remaining
time is computed. `server_ts` is the server's clock.

A supervisor gets every row and punch that day (at their sites, when their
roles name sites; another `site_code` is `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`). Anyone else
gets the roster rows the list route shows them, and only their own punches.
`whole_floor` says which. `site_code` narrows the roster rows only. Punches
from the caller's other sites still appear, as `is_unscheduled` rows.
At most 2000 roster rows are read.

`match_filter_dict` adds conditions on the roster rows. Its
`shift_date_str` and `status` are replaced, and its `site_code` too when
`site_code` is sent.

Refusals: `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_DATE_INVALID`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`,
`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_LOOKUP_FAILED` (the roster read failed),
`PUNCH_LOOKUP_FAILED` (the punch read failed).

post.summary: One day's roster as a PDF
post.description:
`shift_date_str` is required (`SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_DATE_INVALID`). Reads the
caller's visible rows for that day, without cancelled rows. Times render in
each row's own timezone, and an overnight row is marked "+1 day". A day with
no shifts still returns a PDF. A rendering failure is `ROSTER_PDF_FAILED`.
At most 2000 rows are read. `match_filter_dict` adds conditions, but its
`shift_date_str` and `status` are replaced, and its `site_code` too when
`site_code` is sent.

post.summary: Arm or retract a shift reminder
post.description:
Your own row needs no privilege. Someone else's needs `U` on
`shift_assignment` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE`). Someone else's row at a
site the caller does not manage is `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`.

The reminder is a server-side scheduled task. When it fires, the delivery
step reads the roster row again. It sends nothing when the row is gone, the
reminder is off, the shift is cancelled or the shift has started. When the
shift has moved later, it schedules itself again. Delivery is push,
websocket and connected third-party apps. No email or text is sent.

Arming does not check the row's status. A draft or cancelled row is
armed, and delivery then sends nothing.

`lead_minutes` is clamped to 5–1440. Refusals: `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND`,
`SHIFT_HAS_NO_START_TIME`, `SHIFT_STARTS_TOO_SOON` (the fire time is already
past), `REMINDER_NOT_SCHEDULED`.

enabled.description: Send a JSON boolean. Only false, 0, "no" and "none" turn it off, so "off" arms it.

200.description: Envelope with `shift_assignment_id` and `reminder_enabled`, plus `reminder_lead_minutes` and `fire_at_ts` when enabled

post.summary: Record one clock event
post.description:
`direction` may be omitted. The server then toggles from the employee's last
punch: `in` to `out`, `out` to `in`, `break_start` to `break_end`,
`break_end` to `out`, and `in` when there is no punch.

A break is always asked for. Send `break_start` to begin one, because the
toggle never produces it.

**`client_punch_id` is the idempotency key.** A repeat of a stored key
returns the stored punch with `idempotent_replay: true` and writes nothing,
when that punch is still the employee's latest and the request names its
direction or none. A request that sends the stored punch's own reported
`punch_ts` also replays. Otherwise the key is refused with `PUNCH_KEY_SUPERSEDED`,
carrying `latest_direction` and `latest_punch_ts`. `PUNCH_CHECK_FAILED` means
the check could not run and nothing was written.

**Clock-in near the site.** A site can allow clock-in only nearby
(`clock_in_near_site` on the tenant's site, with its coordinates). Then
your own clock-in with `source: mobile` (the default here) is refused
when the roster row is at that site. With no usable `latitude` and
`longitude` the refusal is `CLOCK_IN_LOCATION_NEEDED` with `data`
`{radius_m}`. Farther than the radius is `CLOCK_IN_TOO_FAR` with `data`
`{distance_m, radius_m}`. The radius is the shift definition's
`geofence_radius_m`, at least 161, or 805 (0.5 miles) when it is 0.
Clock-out, breaks, other sources, clocking someone else and a punch with
no roster row are not refused. `policy.clock_in_near_site` on `/status`
tells the app to send its location. An idempotent replay is answered
before this check.

Apart from that, the clock does not refuse a punch for a missing roster
row, a geofence miss or missing evidence. Those are returned in
`exception_list`:
`unscheduled`, `geofence_violation`, `location_missing`, `photo_missing`,
`verification_missing` (the row requires `device_biometric`),
`duplicate_suppressed` (same direction within 90 seconds of the latest
punch; stored with `status: duplicate`) and `unscheduled_at_site`.

`punch_ts` may be sent (epoch seconds or ISO 8601). More than 5 minutes in
the future is `PUNCH_TS_IN_FUTURE`. More than 7 days back is
`PUNCH_TS_TOO_OLD`.

Clocking yourself needs no privilege. Clocking someone else needs `C` on
`punch_event` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE`). A caller whose roles name
sites may clock someone else only when that person belongs at one of their
sites (`EMPLOYEE_NOT_AT_YOUR_SITE`). For that caller, a malformed or unknown
id is also `EMPLOYEE_NOT_AT_YOUR_SITE`. A person with no roster row there is
recorded at the caller's site and flagged `unscheduled_at_site`.

Other refusals: `PUNCH_DIRECTION_INVALID`, `PUNCH_SOURCE_INVALID`,
`PUNCH_VERIFICATION_INVALID`, `PUNCH_VERIFICATION_NOT_SELF_SERVICE`,
`BREAK_TYPE_INVALID`, `PUNCH_TS_INVALID`, `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`,
`EMPLOYEE_USERID_INVALID`, `EMPLOYEE_LOOKUP_FAILED` (the user read failed),
`PUNCH_DUPLICATE` (a punch with the same `client_punch_id` was written at
the same moment and could not be read back).

200.description: Envelope with `punch_event_id`, `punch_event`, `exception_list`, `idempotent_replay` and `message` ("Punch recorded" or "Already recorded")

post.summary: Current clock state, and the shift's verification policy
post.description:
Derived from the employee's last punch. `employee_userid` defaults to the
caller. Another employee needs `R` on `punch_event`
(`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE`), and a caller whose roles name sites sees
only people at those sites (`EMPLOYEE_NOT_AT_YOUR_SITE`).

`policy` is read off the roster row the current time falls in. Failing that,
it uses the row whose start is nearest to now. Only rows that start within
the next 4 hours or ended within the last 4 hours count. With no such row,
every requirement is false and `source` is `default`.

`can_clock_others` is true when the caller has `C` on `punch_event` (a real
admin only, on a tenant with role hierarchy off).

post.summary: Mint this user's badge QR
post.description:
A signed token for the caller, valid for 90 seconds. It carries the caller
(`u`), the tenant (`t`), a nonce (`n`), the claimed `verification` (`v`), and
the caller's `lat`, `lon` and `acc` when sent. There is no parameter for
another person.

The token carries `typ: wf_badge`. `/scan` refuses a token without it. The
nonce becomes the punch's `client_punch_id`. Scanning the same badge again
replays the first punch while it is still the employee's latest.

`verification` accepts the self-service values. Refusals:
`PUNCH_VERIFICATION_INVALID`, `PUNCH_VERIFICATION_NOT_SELF_SERVICE`.

post.summary: Clock the employee named by a scanned badge (terminal)
post.description:
**Direction is not accepted.** It is toggled from the employee's last punch,
by the same rule as `POST /user/punch_event/clock`. A scan after a
`break_end` records `out`, so a badge site can close the day. A scan never
starts a break.

Location: the position sealed in the badge wins, stamped
`location_source: employee_device`. Without one, the terminal's `latitude`
and `longitude` are used, stamped `location_source: terminal`.

`source` is `kiosk`, `mobile` or `terminal` (default `terminal`).

Returns the punch plus `scan_display`: the employee's name, avatar URL,
direction, `work_shift_name`, and `scheduled` (false when the punch carries
`unscheduled`).

Clocking somebody else needs `C` on `punch_event`, so a terminal must be
signed in as an account that has it.

An expired badge whose nonce already has a punch replays that punch, while
it is still the employee's latest punch. After a later punch it is
`PUNCH_KEY_SUPERSEDED`. An expired badge with no punch is `BADGE_EXPIRED`.

default.description:
`BADGE_TOKEN_REQUIRED` · `BADGE_EXPIRED` · `BADGE_INVALID` (not a badge,
or not signed by this server) · `BADGE_WRONG_TENANT` (a badge from
another tenant) · `PUNCH_SOURCE_INVALID` · `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE` ·
`PUNCH_KEY_SUPERSEDED` · `PUNCH_CHECK_FAILED` ·
`EMPLOYEE_NOT_AT_YOUR_SITE` · `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND` · `ROLE_MISSING`
(these three from the clock path)

post.summary: Break entries, as start/end pairs
post.description:
Pairs `break_start` and `break_end` punches from the punch log, per
employee. Reads the caller's visible punches. Naming another
`employee_userid` needs `R` on `punch_event` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE`).

A break with only one half is returned with `taken: false` and a **null**
`duration_minutes`. Entries are sorted newest first, then paged. At most
2000 break punches are read, and `truncated` says when that limit was hit.

`break_type` and `is_paid` are read from the stored `break_start` punch, not
recomputed. A pair whose start falls outside the window has `break_type:
""`, `break_name: "Break"` and `is_paid: false`.

`date_from` after `date_to`, or a value that is not a number, is
`INVALID_DATE_RANGE`.

200.description:
Envelope with `break_entries`, `total_count`, `page_num`, `page_size`,
`truncated`. Each entry: `employee_userid`, `employee_name`, `break_name`
(Meal, Rest or Break), `break_type`, `is_paid`, `start_ts`, `end_ts`,
`duration_minutes`, `duration_hours`, `taken`, `punch_date_str`,
`site_code`, `shift_assignment_id`, `start_punch_id`, `end_punch_id`.

post.summary: Batch ingest from a terminal
post.description:
For a device that queued punches. Each entry is a clock request with its
own `employee_userid`, `punch_ts` and `client_punch_id`. `source` defaults
to `terminal`. A repeat of a stored key is counted in `replayed_count`. A
refused entry is named by index in `failed` and does not stop the others.

Needs `C` on `punch_event` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_INGEST`). At most 500
entries (`PUNCH_BATCH_TOO_LARGE`). An empty list is `PUNCH_LIST_REQUIRED`.
The 7-day back-dating limit does not apply here.

An entry with no `employee_userid` is a punch for the signed-in account,
which on a terminal is the terminal's own user. Send `employee_userid`
on every entry.

On a tenant without Workforce Pro the call still answers `result: 1`.
Each entry is then in `failed` with `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`.

200.description:
Envelope with `accepted_count`, `accepted_ids`, `replayed_count`,
`replayed_ids`, `failed_count`, `failed` (`[{index, employee_userid,
client_punch_id, error_code}]`), `submitted_count` and
`max_batch_size` (500). A `PUNCH_KEY_SUPERSEDED` row also carries
`latest_direction` and `latest_punch_ts`. An entry that is not an
object is `{index, error_code: PUNCH_MALFORMED}`. An unexpected failure
is `{index, employee_userid, error_code: PUNCH_FAILED}`.

post.summary: List or correct punches
post.description:
`action`: `add` | `update` | `delete` | `get` | `get_entity_ids`.
`update`, `delete` and a single `get` name the row with a top-level
`punch_event_id`.

`get` needs no privilege and returns the caller's visible punches, newest
first. `add`, `update` and `delete` need `C`, `U` and `D` on `punch_event`
(`NOT_AUTHORIZED_TO_EDIT_PUNCH`).

`add` records a punch through the clock path with `source` defaulting to
`manual`, as `POST /user/punch_event` does. On a tenant with role hierarchy
off, only a real admin may `add` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_PUNCH_EVENT`). A punch
for yourself keeps the `/clock` limits: `PUNCH_TS_TOO_OLD` and
`PUNCH_VERIFICATION_NOT_SELF_SERVICE`. `update` may change `punch_ts`,
`direction`, `break_type`, `status` and `notes`. `break_is_paid` is derived
from `break_type` by the server. Sending `direction` derives both again, so
a punch moved off `break_start` carries no break kind away.
Changing `punch_ts` needs `edit_reason` (`PUNCH_EDIT_REASON_REQUIRED`), keeps
the first reported time in `original_punch_ts`, and sets `is_edited`,
`edited_by_userid` and `edited_ts`.

A punch on a locked register day cannot be updated or deleted
(`ATTENDANCE_DAY_LOCKED`). A caller whose roles name sites edits only punches
at those sites (`EMPLOYEE_NOT_AT_YOUR_SITE`). A list read caps `page_size`
at 500.

Other refusals: `PUNCH_EVENT_ID_REQUIRED`, `PUNCH_EVENT_ID_INVALID`,
`PUNCH_EVENT_NOT_FOUND`, `PUNCH_STATUS_INVALID`, `PUNCH_DIRECTION_INVALID`,
`PUNCH_EDIT_REASON_REQUIRED`, `ATTENDANCE_LOCK_CHECK_FAILED` (the lock
could not be read).

200.description: Standard envelope keyed `punch_event`. A `delete` with `ids_list` returns `deleted_ids`, `refused` (`[{punch_event_id, error_code}]`) and `deleted_count`.

get.summary: Compact punch list for pickers (query string)
get.description:
The same as POST, with the arguments in the query string. This is what the
web app's reference picker sends. Object arguments are JSON. Before
2026-09-30 this route answered 405 to GET, and the picker showed an empty list.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: JSON object. A value that does not parse as an object is dropped, and the list comes back unfiltered.

parameters.name: sort_dict
parameters.description: JSON object. Accepted and ignored: the order is fixed, as for POST.

post.summary: Compact punch list for pickers
post.description: Newest first. `page_size` is capped at 500.

post.summary: Compute the register for a day (or a range)
post.description:
One day: `employee_userid` and `work_date_str`, both sent. Without both,
the call is read as a range. A range: `from_date_str` and
`to_date_str` (at most 62 days, else `DATE_RANGE_TOO_LARGE`), optionally
narrowed by `employee_userid_list`. A range processes each person and date
that has a punch or a non-cancelled roster row, and each day whose shift
approved time off removed.

A day with no punches inside the person's approved time off is `leave`
with `absence_is_authorized: true`, never `absent`.

Re-processing updates the existing day and leaves `manual_adjust_minutes`
unchanged. It marks the day's punches `processed` and the roster row
`completed`.

A **locked** day is refused with `ATTENDANCE_DAY_LOCKED`. In a range,
locked days are listed in `skipped` and other refusals in `failed`.
`force` is accepted and changes nothing.

On a tenant without Workforce Pro, one day is refused with
`WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`. A range answers `result: 1`, with each day in
`failed` carrying `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`.

**Only unpaid break time comes off the hours.** A break's kind is read from
its `break_start` punch. `break_is_paid` is true for `rest` and false for
`meal`, `other` and a break sent with no type.

Paid punched minutes are capped at the shift's `paid_break_minutes`.
Minutes over that allowance become unpaid break, come off the hours, and
add the `break_over_allowance` exception to the day. A day with no shift
has no allowance, so every punched break on it is unpaid.

Deduction, when an unpaid break was punched: the punched unpaid minutes.
When a break punch is left unpaired, the larger of the punched unpaid
minutes and the shift's `unpaid_break_minutes`. With no unpaid break punch,
the shift's `unpaid_break_minutes`. A break end with no start counts as an
unpaid break punch.

The day's `paid_break_minutes` is the capped punched paid time when the day
has break punches. With no break punches it is the shift's
`paid_break_minutes`. Daily overtime is applied here.

`auto_clock_out` on the shift definition closes an open span at the roster
row's `end_ts` when that time is past and after the first clock-in. The day
is stamped `auto_clocked_out` and flagged `auto_clock_out`. Without it an
open span adds no minutes and is flagged `missing_punch`.

Needs `C` on `attendance_day` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_TO_PROCESS`). A caller whose
roles name sites processes only days at those sites. A range leaves other
sites' days out. One day at another site is `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`. An
unreadable `work_date_str` is `WORK_DATE_INVALID`. A missing or
unreadable range is `DATE_RANGE_INVALID`. So is a request with
`work_date_str` and no `employee_userid`, or `employee_userid` and no
`work_date_str`, because it is read as a range.

work_date_str.description: Send YYYY-MM-DD with zero padding. A form such as "2026-8-24" or a timestamp is accepted, stored as sent, and matches no punches.

200.description:
One day: `attendance_day_id` and `attendance_day`. A range:
`processed_count`, `processed_ids`, `skipped_count`, `skipped`,
`failed_count`, `failed` (`[{employee_userid, work_date_str,
error_code}]`), `days_in_range`, `targets` and `max_days` (62).

post.summary: List, adjust, approve, approve overtime, lock or unlock register days
post.description:
`action`: `get` | `get_entity_ids` | `adjust` | `approve` | `unapprove` |
`approve_overtime` | `unapprove_overtime` | `lock` | `unlock`. Name one day
with a top-level `attendance_day_id`, or several with `ids_list`.

`get` needs no privilege and returns the caller's visible days. `adjust`,
`approve`, `unapprove`, `approve_overtime`, `unapprove_overtime` and `lock`
need `U` on `attendance_day`. **`unlock` needs both `U` and `D`.** Refusals:
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_REGISTER`, and for `unlock` also
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_TO_UNLOCK`. A missing id is `ATTENDANCE_DAY_ID_REQUIRED`,
and a malformed one is `ATTENDANCE_DAY_ID_INVALID`.

`absence_is_authorized` on `adjust` and `approve_overtime` on `approve`
are read as true for any non-empty value. Send JSON booleans: the string
"false" counts as true.

| Action | Payload | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `adjust` | `manual_adjust_minutes`, `adjustment_reason`, `remarks`, `status`, `absence_is_authorized` | Reason required (`ADJUSTMENT_REASON_REQUIRED`). A missing adjustment is 0. A decimal number is cut to a whole number. Text that is not a whole number is `ADJUSTMENT_MINUTES_INVALID`. Worked + adjustment below 0 is `ADJUSTMENT_EXCEEDS_WORKED`. An unknown `status` is `ATTENDANCE_STATUS_INVALID`. Refused on a locked day. |
| `approve` | `approve_overtime` | Sets `is_approved`, `approved_by_userid` and `approved_ts`. With `approve_overtime: true` it also sets `ot_approved`, `ot_approved_by_userid` and `ot_approved_ts`. Refused on a locked day. |
| `unapprove` | | Clears `is_approved`, `approved_by_userid` and `approved_ts`. The overtime approval stays as it is. Refused on a locked day. |
| `approve_overtime` | | Sets `ot_approved`, `ot_approved_by_userid` and `ot_approved_ts`. Leaves `is_approved`, `approved_by_userid` and `approved_ts` as they stand. The day need not be approved. Refused on a locked day. |
| `unapprove_overtime` | | Clears `ot_approved`, `ot_approved_by_userid` and `ot_approved_ts`. The day's own approval stays as it is. Refused on a locked day. |
| `lock` | `payroll_batch_id` | The day must be approved (`ATTENDANCE_DAY_NOT_APPROVED`). |
| `unlock` | `unlock_reason` | Reason required (`UNLOCK_REASON_REQUIRED`). Logged in `meta.unlock_log`. |

**Choosing between `approve` and `approve_overtime`.** On a day that is
already approved, `approve` rewrites `approved_by_userid` and `approved_ts`.
`approve_overtime` leaves the day's approval intact. Use it to sign off
overtime on a day somebody else approved.

The refusal message for `approve_overtime` reads "You do not have permission
to approve overtime on attendance records". For `unapprove_overtime` it reads
"You do not have permission to remove the overtime approval on attendance
records". The `error_code` and the `action` field in the response carry the
wire value.

With `ids_list`, each day is handled on its own, and the response is
`{action, succeeded_ids, succeeded_count, refused: [{attendance_day_id,
error_code}], refused_count}`. A caller whose roles name sites acts only on
days at those sites (`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`). A list read caps `page_size` at
500.

200.description: `get` and `get_entity_ids` return an `attendance_day` array and `total_count` (this schema). Another action on one day returns `attendance_day_id` and one `attendance_day` object. With `ids_list`, the bulk shape above.

get.summary: Compact register list for pickers (query string)
get.description:
The same as POST, with the arguments in the query string. This is what the
web app's reference picker sends. Object arguments are JSON. Before
2026-09-30 this route answered 405 to GET, and the picker showed an empty list.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: JSON object. A value that does not parse as an object is dropped, and the list comes back unfiltered.

parameters.name: sort_dict
parameters.description: JSON object. Accepted and ignored: the order is fixed, as for POST.

post.summary: Compact register list for pickers
post.description: `page_size` is capped at 500.

post.summary: Hours, overtime and lateness totals over a range
post.description:
`group_by` is `employee` (default) or `date` (`GROUP_BY_INVALID`).

**A supervisor totals other people. Everyone else totals themselves.** A
supervisor is a tenant admin, or a holder of `U` on `shift_assignment`, or
a holder of `U` on `attendance_day`.

For a caller who is not a supervisor, an empty or absent
`employee_userid_list` answers with their own rows. Their own userid alone
is also accepted. Naming anybody else is `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_REGISTER`.
`R` on `attendance_day` does not lift this: the seeded employee role holds
`R`. A caller whose roles could not be read gets `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` or
`ROLE_MISSING`.

A caller without `R` on `attendance_day` also gets their own rows. Naming
anyone else is `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE`, refused by the handler before
the rules above run.

A supervisor whose roles name sites gets days at those sites, days with no
site of people whose roles name those sites, and their own. A missing or
unreadable date is `DATE_RANGE_INVALID`. `from_date_str` after
`to_date_str` answers `result: 1` with empty `rows`.

employee_userid_list.description: Send an array. A string is read one character at a time.

post.summary: Apply weekly overtime across one employee's week
post.description:
The week is `week_start_date_str` and the 6 days after it. The threshold is
the smallest `ot_after_weekly_minutes` among that week's shift definitions
with `ot_basis` `weekly` or `both`. Minutes over it become overtime on the
last days of the week first. A day's existing daily overtime is never
reduced. Locked days are left unchanged and counted in `skipped_locked`.

Needs `U` on `attendance_day` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_TO_PROCESS`, or
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_REGISTER` on a tenant with role hierarchy off). A missing
or unreadable `week_start_date_str` is `WORK_DATE_INVALID`. A day at a site
the caller does not manage is `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`.

employee_userid.description: Not checked. Without it no days are found, and the answer is `{"result": 1, "updated_count": 0, "skipped_locked": 0, "weekly_overtime_minutes": 0, "message": "Updated 0 day(s)"}`.

200.description: Envelope with `updated_count`, `skipped_locked`, `weekly_overtime_minutes`, and `week_worked_minutes` and `threshold_minutes` when a weekly policy applies. With days but no weekly policy, `note` says so.

post.summary: Raise, list or withdraw a change request
post.description:
`action`: `add` | `get` | `withdraw`.

`request_type` (default `drop`): `drop` (take me off
`shift_assignment_id`), `pickup` (put me on `requested_work_shift_id` on
`requested_shift_date_str`), or `swap` (both).

**Future shifts only**, on both sides: `SHIFT_ALREADY_STARTED`,
`REQUESTED_SHIFT_NOT_IN_FUTURE`.

Raising one for **yourself** needs no privilege. Raising one for someone else
(`payload.employee_userid`) needs `C` on `shift_assignment` at the sites the
request touches. The shift given up must belong to the person the request is
for (`NOT_YOUR_ASSIGNMENT`). One pending request per shift per person
(`REQUEST_ALREADY_OPEN`).

`get` returns the caller's own requests. A supervisor gets every request
(at their sites, when their roles name sites, plus their own).
`whole_tenant` in the response says which. `get` caps `page_size` at 200. A
top-level `shift_change_request_id` reads one.

`withdraw` (top-level `shift_change_request_id`) works only on a pending
request (`REQUEST_ALREADY_DECIDED`). Withdrawing someone else's request needs
`U` on `shift_assignment`.

200.description: `get`: a `shift_change_request` array, `total_count`, `whole_tenant`, `page_num` and `page_size` (this schema). `add`: `shift_change_request_id` and `shift_change_request` as one object. `withdraw`: `shift_change_request_id` and `status: withdrawn`.

post.summary: Approve or deny, and on approve apply the roster change
post.description:
**Approving applies the change in the same call.** A pickup creates a
`published` roster row. A drop cancels the shift. A swap creates the new row
first, then cancels the old one, and deletes the new row again if the cancel
fails.

Needs `U` on `shift_assignment` for both answers (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_ROSTER`).
Approving a pickup or swap also creates a row, which needs `C`. On this route,
a refusal from creating that row (for example `SHIFT_ASSIGNMENT_OVERLAP`)
carries its code in `error.error_code`. The top-level `error_code` is then
built from the message. `PATCH /user/shift_change_request/{id}` returns the
code as `error_code`. Nobody
decides their own request (`CANNOT_DECIDE_OWN_REQUEST`). A caller whose
roles name sites decides only requests at those sites (`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`).

Approving checks again that the shift has not started
(`SHIFT_ALREADY_STARTED`, `REQUESTED_SHIFT_NOT_IN_FUTURE`) and still
belongs to the requester (`REQUEST_OUTDATED`). Denying skips those checks.

`backfill_required` is true when an approved drop cancelled a shift and
created none. The server does not fill it.

A decided request cannot be decided again (`REQUEST_ALREADY_DECIDED`). A
request whose shift has ended is closed as `expired` first (this one
request only), and deciding it is refused with `REQUEST_EXPIRED`: "This request closed because
the shift ended." A request whose roster row was deleted is refused with
`REQUEST_SHIFT_REMOVED`: "This request closed because the shift was
removed." Withdrawing one is refused the same way.

The decision is written only while the request is still `pending`. When
an expiry, a withdraw or another decision lands first, the loser is
refused: `REQUEST_EXPIRED` if the expiry won, `REQUEST_ALREADY_DECIDED`
otherwise. An approval claims the request before it changes the roster;
if the roster change fails, the request goes back to `pending`. If the
server stops between the claim and the roster change, the hourly job
settles the request after 10 minutes from what the roster shows: the
change is recorded when it happened, and the request goes back to
`pending` when it did not. A swap that got half way through is undone,
and the request goes back to `pending` for a supervisor to answer again.
Every undo write is guarded on this request's own mark, so a row someone
changed since is left alone; a half that cannot be undone safely is left
as it stands for a person to sort out.

approve.description: Send a JSON boolean. Only false, 0, "no" and "none" deny. Any other value, or none, approves and changes the roster.

200.description: Envelope with `status` and `roster_changed`, plus the approve fields

post.summary: Which roster rows have an open request
post.description:
One call for a whole roster page. At most 200 ids are read. Requests whose
shift has ended are not open, whether or not the server has closed them
yet. This read writes nothing.
A crew member gets answers only for their own shifts. A supervisor whose roles name sites
gets answers only for shifts at those sites and their own.

200.description: Envelope with `open_requests` keyed by assignment id

get.summary: Who am I. Supervisor flags, action flags and sites
get.description:
Roles are read from the database on every call. `can` flags are all false
for a caller who is not a supervisor (a tenant admin, or `U` on
`shift_assignment`).

| flag | From |
|---|---|
| `shift_create` / `shift_update` / `shift_delete` | `shift_assignment` C / U / D |
| `clock_others` | `punch_event` C |
| `decide_drops` | `shift_assignment` U |
| `decide_pickups`, `decide_requests` | `shift_assignment` U and C |
| `shift_definition_create` / `_update` / `_delete` | `work_shift` C / U / D, site scoped |
| `crew_manage` | being a supervisor; crews are managed at the caller's sites |

`modules` carries the letters (`C`, `R`, `U`, `D`, `A`) for
`shift_assignment`, `punch_event`, `shift_change_request`, `work_shift`,
`attendance_day` and `time_off`. Deciding time off takes `U` on
`shift_assignment`, the same as `decide_drops`.

`sites`: for an all-sites supervisor, the tenant's sites; for a supervisor
whose roles name sites, those sites; for anyone else, the sites their roles
name.

Refusals: `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` (retry), `ROLE_MISSING`.

post.summary: The roster at a site. Day, Week, By person, By shift
post.description:
Every shift at one site over a window of at most 42 days. `from_date` is
required; `to_date` defaults to it. Optional filters, in any combination:
`employee_userid` (By person), `work_shift_id` (By shift), `crew_id` (shifts
assigned through that crew). An all-sites supervisor may omit `site_code`
to read every site. At most 2000 shifts are returned, and `truncated` says
when more exist.

A supervisor whose roles name sites must send one of them as `site_code`.

**A crew member who is not a supervisor may ask only for themselves**:
`employee_userid` equal to their own id. They get their own shifts at any
site, never a draft, no walk-ins and an empty `staffing`. Anything else is
`NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`.

`live` is present on today's non-cancelled shifts: `{state, clock_in_ts}`,
where `state` is `not_started`, `on_the_clock`, `on_break`, `late`,
`no_show` or `done`. `walk_ins` lists people clocked today with
`unscheduled_at_site` at the site, when the window includes today:
`{employee_userid, employee_name, site_code, clock_in_ts, state,
punch_count}`. `timezone` is the site's `timeZone` from the tenant's site
list, else the tenant's.

**Headcount.** `staffing` lists shift definitions by day:
`{work_shift_id, work_shift_name, shift_date_str, people_needed,
people_count, short_by}`, sorted by date then name. It covers every
definition and day that has a row in this read, and with `work_shift_id`
also every day in the window the definition runs on when it has
`people_needed`. `people_count` is distinct people on a non-cancelled shift
(drafts count) at `site_code` (every site when none), whatever
`search_text`, `include_drafts`, `include_cancelled`, `employee_userid` or
`crew_id` leave in `shifts`. `short_by` is `people_needed - people_count`
when above zero, else 0 (and 0 with no `people_needed`).

Refusals: `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RANGE_TOO_LONG`,
`DATE_RANGE_INVALID`, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ROLE_MISSING`.

search_text.description: Matches the employee name, case and accents folded

200.description: `{result, timezone, today, from_date, to_date, shift_count, truncated, walk_ins, shifts: [{id, employee_userid, employee_name, work_shift_id, work_shift_name, shift_date_str, start_ts, end_ts, site_code, status, assignment_type, notes, cancel_reason, timezone, crosses_midnight, job_title, crew_id, crew_name, recurrence_group_id, scheduled_minutes, times_overridden, start_time_min_override, end_time_min_override, live?}], staffing: [{work_shift_id, work_shift_name, shift_date_str, people_needed, people_count, short_by}]}`

get.summary: People a supervisor can put on a shift at a site
get.description:
Active users holding a role that names the site (`source: role`), plus
anyone with a non-cancelled shift there in the window (`source: scheduled`).
With `include_unsited=true`, also users who hold at least one role, whose
roles name no site and grant no supervisor rights, tenant admins excepted
(`source: unsited`). A user with no role is left out. An
all-sites supervisor who omits `site_code` gets every active user
(`source: tenant`).

The window is `from_date` / `to_date` (one alone is used for both), default
14 days back to 27 days ahead, at most 42 days. `search_text` matches the
name only. At most 200 people are returned, and `truncated` says when more
exist.

Refusals: `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RANGE_TOO_LONG`,
`DATE_RANGE_INVALID`, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ROLE_MISSING`.

200.description: `{result, people: [{userid, name, email_masked, source, is_guest}], truncated}`

get.description:
A supervisor gets the crews at their sites (every site for an all-sites
supervisor) plus any crew they are in. Anyone else gets only the crews they
are a member of. Active crews unless `include_inactive=true`; active first,
then by name. `search_text` matches the name, case and accents folded.
There is no paging. At most 2000 crews are read, with no `truncated`
flag, and `total_count` is the number returned.
Refusals: `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ROLE_MISSING`.

post.summary: Create a crew
post.description:
Needs a supervisor at `site_code`. Rules, each a refusal:

| error_code | data | When |
|---|---|---|
| `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR` | | caller is not a supervisor |
| `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED` | | not one of the caller's sites (a blank site too, for a supervisor whose roles name sites) |
| `SITE_CODE_INVALID` | | not an active registered site, when the tenant has active sites |
| `CREW_NAME_REQUIRED` | | blank |
| `CREW_NAME_TOO_LONG` | `{max_length}` | over 80 characters |
| `CREW_NAME_EXISTS` | | an active crew at this site has the same name (case, accents and spaces folded) |
| `CREW_MEMBERS_INVALID` | | not a list of user ids |
| `CREW_TOO_MANY_MEMBERS` | `{max_members}` | over 200 |
| `CREW_MEMBER_NOT_AT_SITE` | `{userid}` | not an active user of this tenant, or works at other sites and not this one: every one of their roles that names a site names another, and they have no shift here in the last 14 or next 27 days. A person whose roles name no site is at every site. A tenant admin is at every site, and on a tenant with role hierarchy off everyone is. |
| `CREW_LEAD_NOT_A_MEMBER` | `{userid}` | the lead is not in `member_userid_list` |
| `CREW_NOTES_TOO_LONG` | `{max_length}` | over 2000 characters |

A person may be in several crews. Response: `{result: 1, message: "Created",
crew: {...with notes}}`.

parameters.name: crew_id
parameters.description: 24-character hex id. Anything else does not match the route.

get.description: For a supervisor at the crew's site or a member of the crew. Anyone else, and a crew of another tenant, gets `CREW_NOT_FOUND`.

patch.description:
Any of `name`, `lead_userid` (`""` clears it), `member_userid_list` (the whole
new list), `notes`, `is_active`. Same refusals as create. Only people being
added are checked against the site. `site_code` cannot change
(`CREW_SITE_CANNOT_CHANGE`). Setting `is_active: true` on an archived crew is
`CREW_NAME_EXISTS` when an active crew has taken the name. A supervisor who
can read the crew as a member but does not manage its site gets
`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`.

delete.description: When any shift carries this crew it is archived (`is_active: false`, kept so those shifts still resolve), otherwise deleted. Needs a supervisor at its site.

get.description:
`mfa_active` is true when at least one factor gates sign-in. A factor in
`pending_verify` does not. Destinations are masked.

When the factors cannot be read, the answer is HTTP 500 with
`{"result": 2, "error_code": "MFA_LIST_ERROR", "error_message": "..."}`.

post.summary: Turn on one-time-code verification, or confirm it
post.description:
Four operations, chosen by `mfa_type`.

| `mfa_type` | What it does |
|---|---|
| `email` | Enrolls `email` (default: the account's email) in `pending_verify` and **sends a code**. Any existing email factor is removed. The account's email must be confirmed. |
| `email_verify` | Confirms that code and makes the email factor active. |
| `sms` | Enrolls `phone_number` in `pending_verify` and **sends a code**. An existing SMS factor stays until `sms_verify` succeeds. |
| `sms_verify` | Confirms that code and makes the SMS factor active. |

A factor in `pending_verify` does not gate sign-in until its verify call
succeeds.

When the account already has an active factor, `email` and `sms` need
`password` in the body. So do `email_verify` and `sms_verify` when the account
has an active factor of the same type. Refusals: `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`,
`PASSWORD_INCORRECT` (with `attempts_remaining`), and `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` after
too many wrong passwords. An account with no password the owner could know
is not asked: no stored password, or Sign in with Apple and a generated
password.

`phone_number` is sent to the SMS provider in E.164. A number with a leading
`+` keeps its country code. A number without one that has exactly 10 digits
is read as `+1`. An empty value uses the account's phone.

Email codes live for **5 minutes**. `sms` refuses a new enrolment within 30
seconds of the last one (`MFA_RESEND_TOO_SOON`, with
`retry_after_seconds`).

email.description: Optional for `email`; defaults to the account's email.

phone_number.description: Required key for `sms`. Include the country code (E.164).

provider_challenge_id.description: Required for `email_verify` and `sms_verify`, from the enroll response.

challenge_code.description: Required for `email_verify` and `sms_verify`. The code the user received.

password.description: Required when the account already has an active factor (see above).

200.description: On enrollment, `factor_id`, `status`, `provider_challenge_id` and `challenge_destination`; email also returns `expires_at`. Refusals arrive as `{"result": 2}` at HTTP 200: `EMAIL_MFA_REQUIRES_CONFIRMED_EMAIL`, `EMAIL_MFA_NO_EMAIL`, `INVALID_MFA_CODE` (with `attempts_remaining`), `MFA_CHALLENGE_WRONG_PURPOSE`, `INVALID_MFA_TYPE`, `EMAIL_MFA_EXPIRED` (email or SMS), `MFA_CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED`, `EMAIL_MFA_NOT_PENDING` (an email code already used or locked), `MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING` (the same for SMS). A refusal is `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...", "error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string.

delete.description:
`mfa_type` is `email`, `sms` or `all`. `all` removes both. With `sms`, an
optional `factor_id` removes only that factor. Any other value removes
nothing and answers `{"result": 1, "message": "NO-ACTION"}`.

Needs `password` in the body (`PASSWORD_REQUIRED`, `PASSWORD_INCORRECT`,
`ACCOUNT_LOCKED`), with the same exemption as `POST`. The password is
checked for every `mfa_type` value. When no active factor remains, the account's trusted devices are revoked.
A password refusal is `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...", "error_message":
"..."}`, with the message as a plain string.

The fields are read from the **request body**. A body without `mfa_type` is
not handled. It answers HTTP 200 with `result: 2` and `status_code: 500` in
the body.

post.summary: Send a code for a sign-in challenge
post.description:
Called when login returned several factors and the user picked one.
`factor_id` must be one of the factors login offered
(`MFA_FACTOR_NOT_IN_LIST`) and must be active (`MFA_FACTOR_NOT_ACTIVE`).

`pre_mfa_token` is the credential here, because the user has no session yet.
It starts one challenge only: a second call with the same token is
`PRE_MFA_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED` (HTTP 401). To send the code again, call
`POST /user/mfa/verify` with `action: resend`.

Refusals at HTTP 400 or 401: `MISSING_FIELDS`, `INVALID_PRE_MFA_TOKEN`,
`USER_NOT_FOUND`, `MFA_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND`. More than 5 calls a minute from one
IP address answer HTTP 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. At HTTP 200:
`EMAIL_MFA_FACTOR_NOT_ACTIVE`, `EMAIL_MFA_REQUIRES_CONFIRMED_EMAIL` and
`MFA_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`.

Refusals from this handler are `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...",
"error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string. Two use
`error: {message}` instead: `INVALID_JSON` (HTTP 400) for a body that is
not JSON, and `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` or `BOT_DETECTED` from the shared
sign-in check.

post.summary: Enter the code and finish signing in, or resend the code
post.description:
**Verify.** On success the session token is at **`user.token`**. With
`trust_device: true` the response also carries `trust_device_token`. A wrong
code is `INVALID_MFA_CODE` with `attempts_remaining`. The fifth wrong code
ends the challenge with `MFA_CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED`. An expired code is
`EMAIL_MFA_EXPIRED`, for SMS as well. A spent or expired sign-in is
`MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING`. An email code already used or locked is
`EMAIL_MFA_NOT_PENDING`.

**Resend.** `action: resend` with `provider_challenge_id` and `userid` sends a
new code for the same pending sign-in. A resend within 30 seconds of the
previous code is `MFA_RESEND_TOO_SOON` with `retry_after_seconds`. Other
resend refusals: `MFA_NO_FACTORS`, `MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_FOUND`,
`MFA_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND`, `MFA_FACTOR_NOT_ACTIVE`, `MFA_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`.

When the session cannot be issued after a correct code, the answer is
HTTP 500 `LOGIN_RESPONSE_FAILED`. A missing field answers HTTP 400
`MISSING_FIELDS`. More than 5 calls a minute
from one IP address answer HTTP 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

Refusals from this handler are `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...",
"error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string.
`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and `BOT_DETECTED` come from the shared sign-in check
and use `error: {message}`.

action.description: Omit to verify. Any value other than exactly `resend` also verifies.

200.description: Verify: envelope with `user`, including `user.token`. Resend: a new challenge with `is_mfa_response: true`.

post.summary: Enroll and verify a first factor when sign-in requires one
post.description:
Used when `/user/login` returned `requires_mfa_enrollment: true` and an
`enrollment_token`. The token is the credential for this endpoint only.

| `mfa_type` | Body | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | | `verified_contacts`: the email addresses and numbers the account has already proved |
| `email` or `sms` | `contact_id`, optional when the account has exactly one proved contact of that type | Enrolls that contact and sends a code |
| `email_verify` or `sms_verify` | `provider_challenge_id`, `challenge_code`, optional `trust_device`, `device_id`, `os` | Activates the factor and returns the login response, with the token at `user.token` |

Only a contact the account already proved is accepted. Older apps send
`email`, `phone_number` or `phone` in place of `contact_id`. That value is accepted
only when it matches a proved contact. With neither sent and exactly one
proved contact of that type, the server uses it. With two or more, one
must be named. The session is issued only after the
first factor is verified, and the token is then spent. When the session
cannot be issued, the answer is HTTP 500 `LOGIN_RESPONSE_FAILED`.

Refusals: `MFA_ENROLL_NEEDS_VERIFIED_CONTACT` (HTTP 200, with
`verified_contacts`) when the account has no proved contact or the chosen
one does not match, `MISSING_FIELDS` (HTTP 400), `INVALID_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN` (HTTP
401), `USER_NOT_FOUND` (HTTP 401), `INVALID_MFA_TYPE` (HTTP 400),
`INVALID_MFA_CODE` with `attempts_remaining`. More than 10 calls a minute
from one IP address answer HTTP 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

Refusals from this handler are `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...",
"error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string.
`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and `BOT_DETECTED` come from the shared sign-in check
and use `error: {message}`.

get.description:
Paginated read. Shift definitions are created readable by the whole
tenant.

put.summary: Refused. PUT needs an id in the path
put.description: Answers `INVALID_DATA`. Update one work shift at `PUT /user/work_shift/{id}`, which is an alias of PATCH.

get.summary: Refused. Read the collection at the list route
get.description: Answers `NOT_FOUND` with the message "Use GET /user/work_shift/list".

patch.summary: Refused. PATCH needs an id in the path
patch.description: Answers `INVALID_DATA`. Update one work shift at `PATCH /user/work_shift/{id}`.

post.summary: Create a work shift
post.description:
The body **is** the record, with no `action` around it. A `payload` key is
still honoured, so a body from the action endpoint works unchanged.

Response: `{"result": 1, "message": "Created", "work_shift_id": "...",
"work_shift": {...}, "data": {...}}`. `data` is the record read back after
saving. PATCH answers the same shape with `"Updated"`.

Needs `C` on `work_shift`, at a site the caller manages (site scoped; see
DELETE `/user/work_shift/{id}`). Refusals are those of
`POST /user/work_shift/manage`.

200.description: Envelope with `work_shift_id`, the created record under `work_shift`, and `data`: the record read back after saving

delete.description:
Each id is deleted or refused on its own. Response: `{"result": 1, "data":
[{"result": 1, "work_shift_id": "...", "deleted": true} | {"result": 2,
"work_shift_id": "...", "error_code": "...", "error": "...", "data":
{...}}], "deleted_count": n, "refused_count": n}`.

200.description: Envelope reporting what was deleted and what was refused

get.description:
The shift template, with `start_time`, `end_time`, `crosses_midnight`,
`span_minutes`, `template_minutes` and `people_needed` filled in.

200.description: Envelope with the record under `work_shift`, or `{"result": 2, "error_code": "NOT_FOUND"}` when no such record is visible to the caller. A refusal is still HTTP 200.

patch.description:
Partial update. `start_time` / `end_time` accept `HH:MM`. Send
`people_needed: null` (or `""`) to clear the headcount. Needs `U` on
`work_shift`.

200.description: Envelope with `work_shift_id`, the updated record under `work_shift`, and `data`: the record read back after saving

put.summary: Update a work shift (alias of PATCH)
put.description: Same as PATCH: the fields sent are applied one by one.

200.description: Envelope with `work_shift_id`, the updated record under `work_shift`, and `data`: the record read back after saving

delete.description:
Refused when any shift (cancelled ones included) or register day uses this
shift definition:

```json
{"result": 2, "error_code": "WORK_SHIFT_IN_USE",
 "error": {"message": "This shift definition has shifts. Set it inactive instead."},
 "data": {"shift_count": 12}}
```

Set `status: inactive` instead. Success:
`{"result": 1, "data": [{"result": 1, "work_shift_id": "...", "deleted": true}],
"deleted_count": 1, "refused_count": 0}`.

Writes (POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE) need `C` / `U` / `D` on `work_shift` and are
**site scoped**: a caller whose roles name sites writes only definitions at
those sites (`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`), cannot create one at no site, and cannot

get.description:
The queue, newest first by default. A crew member gets their own requests.
A supervisor gets every request (at their sites, when their roles name
sites, plus their own). `whole_tenant` in the response says which.

**Expiry.** A pending request whose shift has ended reads as `expired`.
A drop expires when its roster row ends, with any changed times. A pickup
expires when the wanted shift ends on `requested_shift_date_str`, in that
definition's zone. A swap expires when the first of its two shifts ends. A
night shift from 22:00 to 06:00 stays pending until 06:00. When the roster
row or the wanted definition was deleted, it expires 16 hours after the
end of its shift date.

This read writes nothing. A `{"status": "pending"}` filter and its count
leave out a request whose shift has ended. `{"status": "expired"}` takes it
in, and the row comes back with `status: expired` and an `expired_ts`
(its shift end). A server job writes `expired` once an hour, and a
decision or a withdraw closes its own request first. Until that job has
run once for it, a request made before `expires_at_ts` existed reads
pending for up to two days after its shift date.

**Closed requests.** A caller who reads only their own requests gets an
expired one for 7 days after its `expired_ts`, then no longer. A
supervisor's queue keeps every expired request. A `shift_removed`
request stays in the requester's list with no time limit. A filter
whose `status` names only `expired` and `shift_removed`, with an
`expired_ts` range, reads `shift_removed` rows against
`status_updated_ts`. The Workforce app asks for
`{"status": "expired", "employee_userid": <me>, "expired_ts": {"$gte":
<now - 7 days>}}` and shows the rows as closed. With `status: expired`
alone, that `expired_ts` range also matches a request the job has not
closed yet, by the `expired_ts` it reads with.

get.summary: A pay period as a Toast Payroll custom-import CSV
get.description:
Produces a CSV in the column layout of Toast Payroll's **Custom Import**.

### The shape

Headers, in this order: `EE Number`, `EE Name`, `Job`, `Regular Hours`,
`Overtime Hours`, `Week`. One row per **employee per job per week**. `Week`
is an **ordinal within the pay period** (`1`, `2`, `3`), counted in 7-day
blocks from `from_date_str`. Hours are decimal, rounded to two places. A
group with no payable minutes produces no row. The file is sent as
`toast_hours_<from>_<to>.csv`.

### Regular hours carry the adjustment

In the register, `regular_minutes + overtime_minutes = worked_minutes`, which
excludes `manual_adjust_minutes`. `Regular Hours` is therefore computed from
**payable** minutes (worked + adjustment, floored at zero) less overtime, so
regular + overtime equals payable.

### Payroll numbers

`EE Number` comes from `payroll_employee_number` on the user record. An admin
sets it through `/user/admin/user/update`; `/user/update_profile` ignores it.

When anyone in the period has no payroll number, the export **refuses** with
`PAYROLL_EE_NUMBER_MISSING`. The refusal does not name them. Pass
`allow_missing_ee_number=true` to export anyway with a blank `EE Number`;
`format=json` then lists them in `missing_ee_number`.

A blank `Job` is counted in `warnings.blank_job_rows` and does not refuse.

### Pay

**Pay figures reach a tenant admin only.** For an admin, the JSON response
prices the period when an employee has an `hourly_rate` on their user
record:

```
payout = regular_hours x rate + overtime_hours x rate x ot_multiplier
```

`ot_multiplier` is the highest multiplier recorded on those register days,
or 1.5 when none is recorded. `hourly_rate` and `hourly_rate_currency` are
set by an admin through `/user/admin/user/update`; `/user/update_profile`
ignores them. Pay appears only in `format=json`.

For a supervisor who is not an admin, `hourly_rate` and `payout` are
`null` on every row, `payout_by_currency` is empty, and
`warnings.unpriced_employees` is 0. `currency` is the tenant's. The hours
are the same for both. `pay_rates_included` says which answer this is. The
CSV never carried a rate.

### Access

Needs `R` on `attendance_day` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED`). `R` on its own is not
enough. The caller must also be a **supervisor**: a tenant admin, or a
holder of `U` on `shift_assignment`, or a holder of `U` on
`attendance_day`. Anyone else gets `NOT_AUTHORIZED`. A caller whose roles
could not be read gets `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` or `ROLE_MISSING`.

A caller whose roles name sites exports days at those sites, days with no
site of people whose roles name those sites, and their own. The JSON
response says so in `site_scoped` and `sites`.

Refusals arrive as `{"result": 2}` at HTTP 200: `NOT_AUTHORIZED` without register read access, `INVALID_DATA` for a missing date or an unknown `format`, `DATE_RANGE_INVALID` for an unreadable or inverted range, `PAYROLL_EE_NUMBER_MISSING` when someone in the period is unmapped, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` or `ROLE_MISSING` when the caller's scope cannot be read, and `PAYROLL_EXPORT_FAILED`.

patch.description:
`{"status": "approved" | "denied" | "cancelled", "decision_note": "…"}`.
Supervisor only (`U` on `shift_assignment`), at the person's sites when the
caller's roles name sites. Nobody decides their own
(`CANNOT_DECIDE_OWN_TIME_OFF`).

**`approved` applies in this call.** Every live shift of the person dated
inside the range that has not started and is not in the register is
cancelled, with `cancel_reason: "Time off approved"` and
`cancelled_by_time_off_id`. Pending change requests on those shifts are
withdrawn. From then on any roster write for the person on those days is
refused with `ON_LEAVE`: adding or moving a shift, generate, a substitute
cover, and approving a pickup. The response carries
`cancelled_assignment_ids`, `kept_assignment_ids` (started, left on the
roster) and `backfill_required`. When cancelling fails part way the time
off stays approved, the refusal is `TIME_OFF_SHIFTS_NOT_CANCELLED`, and a
server job removes the rest within the hour.

**`cancelled`** calls off approved time off (`TIME_OFF_NOT_APPROVED`
otherwise). The shifts it removed are not put back:
`shifts_restored: false`.

**The register.** A day inside approved time off with no punches is
processed as `leave` with `absence_is_authorized: true`. Leave days are
zero hours.

Other refusals: `TIME_OFF_ALREADY_DECIDED`, `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`,
`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `TIME_OFF_NOT_FOUND`, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` (the
caller's or the person's roles could not be read). A `status` other than
the three above is `INVALID_DATA`. `note` is read when `decision_note`
is absent.
